instructions: Put 16 bamboo skewers in a shallow dish of water and leave them to soak for at least 30 minutes.
Put the beef in the freezer for 15 minutes. It slices thin much more easily when it's firm.
Meanwhile, peel off the tough outer layers of the lemongrass and mince the pale lower half very fine. Mince 4 of the garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, stir together the lemongrass, the minced garlic, 3 tbsp of the fish sauce, 1 tbsp of the sugar, the black pepper and 2 tbsp of the oil.
Slice the beef across the grain into strips about 1/4 inch thick, 1 inch wide and 2 to 3 inches long. Toss the strips in the marinade and leave them at room temperature for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce. Mince the 2 remaining garlic cloves and juice both limes. That should be about 1/4 cup of juice. Stir the garlic and juice together with the remaining 3 tbsp fish sauce, the remaining 3 tbsp sugar and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves.
Wash and dry the lettuce and tear it into pieces. Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons. Pick the leaves from half the mint and half the cilantro. Arrange them on a platter.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the vermicelli for the time on the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water. Drain well and set aside.

Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, then brush it with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. You can also set a rack 4 inches from the broiler, heat the broiler for 5 minutes and cook the skewers on a foil-lined baking sheet.
Drain the skewers and thread 1 or 2 strips of beef onto each one.
Cook the skewers in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes on the first side. Turn them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, until the beef is browned and a little charred at the edges.
Taste the dipping sauce. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce or a pinch more sugar.
Divide the noodles between 4 bowls. Serve the skewers over the noodles with the lettuce, cucumber and herbs and the dipping sauce.
method_notes: None of the versions found had enough ratings, so this follows Sunset's bo nuong xa toi (fish sauce, garlic, lemongrass, pepper marinade) with Andrea Nguyen's thin 1/4 inch strips and short skewer cooking. Sources marinate 1 to 2 hours; this uses a 20 minute marinade while the sauce and noodles come together, which is why the strips are cut thin. The sources use soy or hoisin in places and peanuts as a garnish; both are left out so it stays gluten-free and nut-free. The dipping sauce is a standard nuoc cham (fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic) as the list's description pairs the skewers with rice noodles.
